meta.name: IrForge — Discord bot builder (phased build plan)
meta.language_of_prompts: English (best for code agents). All end-user UI copy must be Persian-first with the 5 locales.
how_to_use_fa: هر فاز یک پرامپت کامل و خودکفاست (فیلد prompt). فقط همان را بده به Claude Code، یک فاز در هر نوبت.
بعد از هر فاز: خروجی را (فایل‌های تغییرکرده + نتیجه‌ی تست) ببین، دیپلوی کن، دستی امتحان کن، بعد برو فاز بعدی.
فاز را ردیف‌به‌ردیف دنبال کن (depends_on). فازهای هم‌مرحله که depends_on مشترک دارند می‌توانند موازی شوند.
فازهای پرریسک (پرداخت، هوش مصنوعی) فلگ risk دارند؛ قبل از شروع تصمیم بگیر.
قبل از هر مایگریشن روی دیتابیس واقعی، از Postgres بک‌آپ بگیر (این کار با خودت است).

architecture_decisions.decision: Bring-your-own-token: each owner creates a Discord application and pastes its bot token.
architecture_decisions.why: A single shared bot needs Discord verification after 100 servers, has stricter privileged-intent rules and one blast radius. BYO token = each owner's bot is theirs, branded, and limits are per bot (same model as the Telegram side).

architecture_decisions.decision: Separate runtime service `irforge-discord` (Python, discord.py 2.x) built from the irforge-app repo (sub-package `discord_runtime/`, own start command), sharing utils (db pool, token crypto).
architecture_decisions.why: Gateway websockets and caches behave differently from Telegram long-polling; isolating them stops a Discord memory/CPU problem from taking down Telegram bots. Same repo = reuse of utils and one CI.

architecture_decisions.decision: Separate site-DB table `discord_bots` (+ products with category_id='discord' for plans) instead of adding a platform column to `bots`.
architecture_decisions.why: `bots` is deeply Telegram-specific (sheetId/tenant, getMe, usernames, sheet pool). A new table avoids regressions; billing, notifications, audit, wallet and /super are reused.

architecture_decisions.decision: Business data in the business Postgres with RLS, tenant_id = 'd:<discord_bots.id>', plus a guild_id column on guild-scoped tables.
architecture_decisions.why: Same isolation model as Telegram; a purge is `DELETE ... WHERE tenant_id = ...`.

architecture_decisions.decision: Web <-> runtime coordination through Postgres only (no extra broker): `discord_bot_runtime` heartbeat/status table + a `discord_bot_commands` queue claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; runtime reconciles desired vs running bots every few seconds.
architecture_decisions.why: Zero new infrastructure on Railway; works with multiple replicas via leasing.

architecture_decisions.decision: Intents are declared per feature; the runtime requests only what enabled features need. Privileged intents (members, message content) are checked in the connect wizard from the application flags.
architecture_decisions.why: Least privilege, lower memory, fewer owner-side surprises.

owner_decisions_needed: P24 (member-paid roles) moves real money between third parties — check Iranian payment/legal rules and decide whether to use the owner's own gateway merchant id (recommended) before starting it.
P26 (AI assistant) has a per-message LLM cost — decide the provider, per-tier quotas and whether it exists at all.
Plan names and prices for the `discord` product category (suggested: Free (1 server, core features), Standard, Pro) — set in P1, editable later in the admin Products panel.
Discord itself is filtered in Iran: your Railway runtime is fine, but your Iranian customers need a VPN to use Discord; consider this in marketing.
non_goals: Mass DM / self-bot / any feature that sends unsolicited DMs at scale (against Discord ToS; P27 must actively block it).
One shared platform-owned bot for all customers.

shared_context_header:
You are a senior full-stack engineer working on IrForge, an Iranian multi-tenant bot-builder SaaS (Persian-first, RTL). Telegram bots exist today; you are adding a Discord bot builder next to them. Work ONLY on the phase below; do not start other phases.

REPOS (GitHub owner poti222, branch main deploys to Railway):
- irforge-web: pnpm monorepo. `api-server` = Express + TypeScript, bundled with esbuild (`node build.mjs`), tests with node:test via tsx (`test/*.test.mjs`); site DB migrations are idempotent SQL in `api-server/migrate.mjs`, mirrored by `lib/db/migrations/NNNN_*.sql`; `lib/db/src/schema/*.ts` = drizzle schema (export from schema/index.ts); `irforge` = Vite + React + wouter + TanStack Query + shadcn/ui, 5 locales (fa, en, ar, tr, ru) in `irforge/src/locales/*.json` guarded by a key-parity test; API calls go through `customFetch` from `@workspace/api-client-react`.
- irforge-app: Python 3 + aiogram runtime that runs many tenants' Telegram bots in one process. Business data lives in a second Postgres (BUSINESS_DATABASE_URL), every table has `tenant_id` + Row Level Security driven by `set_config('app.tenant_id', ..., true)` per transaction. Tests with pytest.
- Production: Railway services irforge-web, irforge-app, Postgres.

CONVENTIONS (mirror the existing Telegram code for anything analogous; read it BEFORE writing code):
- Prices are integer RIAL in the DB (UI shows Toman = Rial / 10). Wallet debits use the existing wallet helpers; products live in the `products` table (category_id + metadata JSON such as periodDays / autoRenew); money-moving code must be idempotent and audited.
- Secrets: bot tokens are stored encrypted (reuse the existing tokenCrypto scheme in both repos); never log, return or render a token; mask sensitive columns.
- Super-admin screens register in `irforge/src/components/super/superTabs.ts` (and the tab-count test); admin writes go through `writeAudit` (extend the AuditAction union); user notices through `createNotification`.
- Every user-visible string exists in all 5 locales (fa first). FAQ answers must not contain markdown links. Do not "fix" a failing parity test by deleting keys.
- Persian UI copy is the source of truth: casual, clear, RTL-safe (use dir="auto" for user data).
- Small, reviewable commits. Before finishing run: api-server build + tests, irforge build + tests, pytest for irforge-app if touched. Known pre-existing failure you must not hide: localeParity (ar/tr/ru intentionally lack the `schools.*` namespace).
- Do NOT push to main; leave changes on a feature branch named after the phase id and report: files changed, tests run + results, assumptions made, anything blocked or needing a product decision.
- Verify every Discord limit/endpoint/flag you rely on against the CURRENT official Discord developer docs before using it; the numbers in this prompt are a starting point, not truth.

phases.title: Discord runtime skeleton (multi-bot gateway manager)
phases.goal: A separate Python service that can run N Discord bots from their stored tokens with isolation, backoff and clean shutdown — no features yet.
tasks: Create package `discord_runtime/` (discord.py 2.x, asyncio) with its own entrypoint and a `railway.toml`/start command for a NEW Railway service `irforge-discord`; reuse irforge-app utils for the DB pool and token decryption.

`BotSupervisor`: every 5-10 s load `discord_bots` with status in (active) and desired state, start missing clients, stop clients whose bot is stopped/expired/deleted, restart on token change. One `discord.Client` per bot with `chunk_guilds_at_startup=False`, minimal member cache flags and only the intents the bot's enabled features need (a registry `FEATURE_INTENTS`, empty for now besides guilds).

Isolation: an exception in one bot's task never stops others; exponential backoff with jitter per bot; if login fails with an authentication error mark the bot `invalid_token` and stop retrying (the web side notifies the owner in a later phase).

Replica safety: bots are claimed with a lease row (`discord_bot_runtime`: bot_id pk, owner_instance, lease_until, status, last_heartbeat, guild_count, last_error) using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; renew the lease every 15 s; a dead instance's bots are re-claimed after the lease expires.
Health: tiny aiohttp server with /healthz (process alive + db reachable) and /metrics (bots running, guilds, reconnects); graceful SIGTERM (close clients, release leases).
Write `discord_guilds` rows on guild_join/guild_remove/ready (via tenant_tx).
Tests with a mocked discord client factory: start/stop reconciliation, crash isolation, lease takeover, invalid-token handling.
done_when: Service starts locally against a test bot token (documented manual step) and shows the bot online; `discord_guilds` fills for guilds the bot is in.
Killing one bot's task does not affect another in tests; SIGTERM releases leases.
pytest suite for the supervisor passes.
